data.name: Ittihad

in_arabic.name: اتحاد
in_arabic.long_meaning: اتحاد يعني الاتحاد والائتلاف والاتفاق، ومصدره اتحاد الذي يعني جمع الشمل والوحدة، وهو概念 مهم في الإسلام يشير إلى وحدة المسلمين وترابطهم، وهو مرتبط بالروح الإسلامية والتعاون

in_urdu.name: اتحاد
in_urdu.long_meaning: اتحاد کا مطلب ہے یکجہتی اور اتفا ق، اور اس کا ماخذ عربي زبان سے ہے، اس کی جڑیں عربي زبان کی اصطلاح اتحاد سے ملتی ہیں، جو جمع الشمل اور اتحاد کے معنی دیتی ہے، یہ تصور اسلام میں بہت اہم ہے جو مسلم اقوام کی یکجہتی اور ترابط کو ظاہر کرتا ہے

data.cultural_impact: The Islamic term "Ittihad" holds deep significance in the social and cultural fabric of the Islamic world. In the historical context, Ittihad refers to the unity and solidarity among Muslims, symbolizing their collective commitment towards upholding the values and principles of Islam. This concept is particularly echoed in the political domain, where renowned Islamic movements and organizations, such as the Society of the Muslim Brothers or the Islamic State of Iraq and Levant (ISIL), have adopted this term as a key component of their ideology. It embodies a call for unity among Muslim peoples, irrespective of ethnic, linguistic, or regional differences, being rooted in the common bond of belief in the One God and the acceptance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as His Messenger. Furthermore, Ittihad transcends cultural boundaries and is also present in the various Sufi orders, or Tariqas, emphasizing unity between the seeker and the Divine. A powerful cultural symbol, Ittihad is reminders of shared values and an essential reminder of the strength in unity among a diverse and global Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: Ittihad carries profound spiritual significance within the Islamic tradition, serving as a reminder of the ultimate goal of the spiritual journey, i.e., the attainment of unity and oneness with the Divine. According to the Sufi mystics, Ittihad represents the Station of Unity, signifying a soul's union with God and an end to duality and multiplicity between the Creator and the creation. In the Hadith literature, Ittihad is mentioned as one of the fruits of faith, where the believer becomes one with the Divine in the state of "Fana'," - the annihilation of the self in God. This spiritual unification is seen as a prelude to the ultimate union, "Unity in Essence," or "Wahda QStringa," - the state of being one in essence with the Divine. Through highlighting the ideal of unity and oneness in spiritual development, Ittihad ultimately invites individuals to deepen their devotion to God and further their journey in seeking His divine presence.
